chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Qasim ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who stands (for prayer) at the end of the night and he fears that the morning will catch him suddenly; should he begin with Al-Witr, or pray the Salat in its complete form so that Al-Witr becomes the last of that? He said: 'Rather, he should begin with Al-Witr.' And he said: 'I used to do that.'

key_terms.آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ: The end of the night, the time for Tahajjud (night voluntary prayer).
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ عَلَى وَجْهِهَا: The prayer in its complete form, referring to performing the full number of units (rak'ahs) for the voluntary prayer.
key_terms.الْوَتْر: Witr, the odd-numbered prayer performed at the end of the night, considered a confirmed Sunnah.
key_terms.يَفْجَأَهُ الصُّبْحُ: The morning (dawn) catches him suddenly, referring to the fear of missing the Fajr prayer time.

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order of prayers if one fears dawn will arrive during night prayers?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural priority of Witr when time is short, emphasizing its status as the concluding seal of night prayers. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that Witr, while technically optional (Sunnah), holds such significance that it is treated with the urgency of a necessary act to ensure the completion of the night's worship. The Imam’s personal practice serves as a practical model for balancing thoroughness in voluntary acts with the certainty of fulfilling key rituals before the fixed time of Fajr.

en.hubeali:
Al-Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al-Qasim Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about the man who stands (for the Salāt) at the end of the night and he is fearing if the morning comes up suddenly, should he begin with Al-Witr, or pray the Salāt upon its aspects until Al-Witr happens to be at the end of that?’ Heasws said: ‘But, he should begin with Al-Witr’. And heasws said: ‘Iasws was doing that’.
en.sarwar: 28. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Qasim ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who gets up in the end of the night and he is afraid of coming of dawn (before completing). Should he begin with al-Witr or perform Salah (prayer) as normal so that al-Witr becomes the last item?’ He (the Imam) said, ’He begins with al-Witr.’ He (the Imam) said, ’I have done so.’”
